sources: Maestro's first drafts, from the theory core's notes (PLAN.md tasks 2.2 to 2.5)
Progressions: Open Music Theory's loops and schemas (CC BY-SA 4.0) and jazznet's ii-V (MIT), as ideas in our own words (task 3.2)
Tumbao: Wikipedia, "Tumbao" (CC BY-SA 4.0), in our own words (task 3.2)

rhythm.why: Anticipations; everything sits with the clave.

vocabulary.why: ii-Vs and sevenths; the minor key's V7 from harmonic minor.

leading.why: The montuno moves in octaves; smooth inside.

progressions.why: Vamps that loop under the montuno, and ii-V cadences; a section keeps its vamp a long time.

montuno vamp.why: the son montuno's two-bar vamp: home, its subdominant, the dominant, back through iv

minor ii-V.why: the ii-V into home, salsa's cadence, over and over

andalusian.why: four steps down to the dominant

minor circle.chords: i7 | iv7 | bVII7 | bIIImaj7 | bVImaj7 | iiø7 | V7 | i7
minor circle.why: down by fifths through the whole key: the long road home

major montuno.why: the vamp in a major key

major ii-V.why: the ii-V into a major home

major turnaround.why: home, then round the circle back to it

members.why: Piano, acoustic bass, trumpet. The sketch's drum guide is clave and cowbell, so no kicks or hats.

patterns.why: The tumbao: the bass skips the one and plays ahead of the chord.

tumbao.why: on the and of 2 and on 4, each the root of the chord about to sound, held over the one

tumbao with the fifth.why: the and of 2 on the coming chord's fifth, 4 on its root

tumbao on the one.why: the one as well: heavier and plainer

variants.why: Never drop a tumbao note: two is already lean.
